headline: MEAL HOLDS 6% GAIN; TYSON CUTS BEEF FOOTPRINT
subheadline: Soybean meal's overnight move held all day; Tyson's three-plant exit reshapes the fed cattle market heading into fall.
lead: Soybean meal closed at $325.00, holding every cent of its 6% overnight move, the biggest single-session print in months. Meanwhile Tyson Foods announced it will close or sell three beef plants, anchoring around Dakota City, Holcomb, and Amarillo. That's two structural shifts landing on the same Friday: one in the crush, one in the packing chain. Neither is a one-day story.
the_takeaway: Meal held its move; Tyson's exit means fewer bids for fed cattle this fall.
teaser: Meal locked in a 6% gain and Tyson just shrank its beef footprint. Two structural shifts on one Friday.

one_number.unit: Tyson beef plants closing or sold
one_number.context: Tyson is anchoring its beef business around three central-US facilities and shedding the rest. With the Cargill Fort Morgan lockout already pulling roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, another round of plant consolidation tightens the kill capacity picture for fall marketings.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called beans down toward below $11.50; beans closed today at $11.67, up on the day.
yesterdays_call.note: Meal carried beans higher instead; the export catalyst flipped the direction.

sections.title: MEAL HOLDS; BEANS FIRM
sections.body:
- Soybean meal closed at **$325.00**, holding its full 6% overnight move as Argentine crush-margin tightness and fresh export demand kept sellers away all session.
- Soybeans nearby added a token cent and a half to $11.67; the meal/oil split did the real work, with oil giving back 1.1% to $68.88 while meal ran.
- Post-WASDE, the USDA's August supply-demand report handed corn a more supportive read than beans, so beans are leaning on the crush story, not the acreage story, to stay bid.
sections.catalyst: Argentine crush tightness plus USDA August WASDE more supportive for corn than beans.
sections.bottom_line: Meal is the bull leg right now; beans are along for the ride, not leading it.
sections.farmer_action: If you priced old-crop beans near $11.74 yesterday, that worked. New-crop Nov at $11.88 is fair value; let the Pro Farmer tour Aug 17 reset the bid before adding sales.
sections.vs_yesterday: Beans: held the $11.65 floor called yesterday; meal carried the complex.

sections.title: WHEAT RUNS ON URT-LUGA FIRE
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat closed at **$6.67**, up 10.5 cents, a 1.6% gain that put it at 80% of its 52-week range on a day the whole complex was quiet except the crush.
- A Ukrainian drone strike set fire to Ust-Luga, Russia's top Baltic export port for oil and commodities, overnight; the wheat market priced the logistics disruption into the close.
- Funds that had been sitting on the fence in wheat finally had a news hook, and they used it.
sections.catalyst: Ukrainian drone strike sparked fire at Ust-Luga, Russia's top Baltic commodity export port.
sections.bottom_line: Wheat's move is real and news-driven; hold above $6.55 and the chart keeps the funds honest.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: broke above $6.55 resistance called earlier this week on a hard catalyst.

sections.title: CATTLE SLIP; TYSON RESHAPES THE KILL
sections.body:
- Live cattle closed at **$226.22**, down 1.9%, the sharpest single-session drop in weeks, as Tyson's announcement that it will close or sell three beef plants landed during the session.
- Feeders eased to $343.02, off 0.9%; the feeder/live spread is still wide, but Tyson shedding plants means fewer competing bids for finished cattle this fall, not a bullish setup.
- The Cargill Fort Morgan lockout, ongoing since May 19, already pulled roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity; Tyson's move stacks consolidation on top of disruption.
sections.catalyst: Tyson Foods announced closure or sale of three beef plants, anchoring around Dakota City, Holcomb, and Amarillo.
sections.bottom_line: Two packing-chain shocks in one summer: less capacity means longer marketing windows and more price risk for feedlots.
sections.farmer_action: If you have fall-delivery contracts on fed cattle, get clarity on which packer and which plant before harvest. Capacity is tighter than the calendar usually shows.

sections.title: ENERGY FIRMS; HORMUZ TRAFFIC SLUMPS
sections.body:
- WTI crude closed at **$81.69**, up 0.4%, capping a roughly 4% weekly gain as the US-Iran standoff over Hormuz -- re-escalated in mid-July when commercial vessels were struck -- showed no sign of resolution.
- Hormuz tanker crossings fell to five on Wednesday and nine on Thursday; a growing share are going dark with transponders off, signaling the disruption is not easing.
- Diesel, not headline WTI, is the input-cost number for fall fieldwork. Watch the crack spread.
sections.bottom_line: Crude's weekly gain is Hormuz-driven; diesel tightness is the farmer's real number to watch into harvest.

outside_the_pit.title: Senate Farm Bill Markup Stalls; September 30 Deadline at Risk
outside_the_pit.body: FarmDoc Daily reports the Senate Agriculture Committee appears to have driven another nail in the Farm Bill's coffin this week. Year-round E15 and the revised SNAP cost-share language are in the text, but floor passage needs 60 votes and the September 30 extension deadline is closing fast.

outside_the_pit.title: Screwworm Sterile Fly Facility Opens 7 Months Early in Texas
outside_the_pit.body: USDA confirmed a Texas sterile fly breeding facility will open ahead of schedule, accelerating the containment effort that underpins the phased Mexican feeder cattle port reopening set for August 24 at Douglas, AZ. Faster containment means the August 24 date holds; watch feeder spreads as that reopening approaches.

weekly_thread.question: Does the WASDE on Tuesday confirm a record or near-record corn yield, and does that break Dec corn below $4.50?
weekly_thread.status_text: WASDE confirmed a supportive corn read but Dec corn closed the week at $4.76, never testing $4.50; the breakdown thesis didn't play out, and the Pro Farmer tour starting Monday resets the question.

the_more_you_know.title: Meal Runs, Oil Falls: How the Crush Split Prices the Next Bet
the_more_you_know.body: When meal and oil move in opposite directions inside the crush, the market is arguing about where demand lives. Today meal ran 6% and oil gave back 1.1%. That split says biofuel demand is soft relative to protein demand right now. Watch the ratio into next week: if meal holds and oil recovers, the whole bean complex firms. If oil keeps sliding, the crush margin compresses and beans lose their floor.

watch_list.desc: USDA Crop Progress: corn good/excellent above 65% keeps the weather premium stripped; a drop below 60% adds a bid into the Pro Farmer tour.
Pro Farmer Crop Tour begins: corn yield above 184 bu/acre puts pressure on Dec corn; below 182 puts $4.50 back in play.
Weekly Export Sales: meal above 200K MT confirms the export leg of today's rally; below that, it was positioning, not demand.
Douglas, AZ phased Mexican feeder cattle port reopening: watch feeder spreads the week prior; any delay or expansion extends the supply tightness trade.

daily_quote.text: Success is stumbling from failure to failure with no loss of enthusiasm.
